probe.note: The probe re-read the already-known P2-11B Atomic-EVTX suite for calibration analysis. It did not change detector or rule semantics.

evidence: Sysmon Event 1 shows cmd.exe executing gsecdump.exe -a.
No Sysmon Event 10 or other direct credential-access event appears in this five-channel scenario capture.
scenarios.root_cause: The action is visible primarily through a tool-specific process command line. Existing credential-dumping rules target LSASS access, SAM/SYSTEM saves, NTDS, or other narrower behaviors and do not match this invocation.
scenarios.reason: Adding a gsecdump-name rule would be easy but would be strongly tool-specific. Prefer a tool-independent credential-access signal if available before adding coverage.

evidence: Sysmon Event 1 captures the PowerShell command that copies NPPSPY.dll and modifies HKLM SYSTEM CurrentControlSet Control NetworkProvider Order and Services NPPSpy NetworkProvider settings.
This capture contains Sysmon process create/terminate events but no Sysmon registry Event 13 for those changes.
scenarios.root_cause: Credential-capture setup is visible inside a long PowerShell command, but the available capture lacks a direct registry-change event and current rules do not model network-provider credential capture.
scenarios.reason: A rule based on the NPPSpy name would overfit. A broader NetworkProvider configuration rule may be possible, but it needs a benign collision study before use.

scenarios.description: Read volume boot sector via DOS device path (PowerShell)
evidence: Sysmon Event 1 captures PowerShell constructing IO.FileStream for \.\C: with Open and Read and then reading bytes.
scenarios.root_cause: The raw-volume read is present in command-line telemetry, but the 60-rule pack has no T1006 rule for direct volume/device access.
scenarios.reason: The behavior can be described without the Atomic test name, but the candidate must be checked against pinned benign PowerShell/device-path usage before adoption.

evidence: Sysmon Event 1 captures powershell.exe -EncodedCommand with a concrete Base64 payload.
The current Encoded PowerShell rule maps this behavior to T1059.001, which was observed in P2-11B, not to the suite's expected T1027.
scenarios.root_cause: This is primarily an ATT&CK technique-mapping/granularity gap rather than a failure to notice encoded PowerShell.
scenarios.reason: Do not replace the existing PowerShell mapping merely to fit the suite. Consider dual-tagging only if the rule semantics and ATT&CK mapping are independently justified.

evidence: Sysmon Event 1 records sc.exe query and sc.exe query state= all, spawned from cmd.exe.
scenarios.root_cause: Service-discovery command telemetry is clear, but the 60-rule pack has no T1007 rule.
scenarios.reason: A semantic sc.exe query rule is straightforward and not tied to the Atomic scenario name, but benign administrative use must be measured.

evidence: Sysmon Event 1 records net.exe start and the corresponding net1.exe start process chain.
scenarios.root_cause: Service-discovery command telemetry is clear, but the 60-rule pack has no T1007 rule for this form.
scenarios.reason: A net.exe/net1.exe service-listing rule is semantically direct but likely overlaps legitimate administration, so benign measurement is required.

evidence: Sysmon Event 1 captures PowerShell preparing TERMSRV credentials with cmdkey and launching mstsc.exe /v:.
The selected five-channel capture does not include TerminalServices operational channels that would directly prove a completed RDP session.
scenarios.root_cause: RDP client invocation is visible, but the existing T1021.001 rule focuses on enabling/configuring RDP rather than mstsc client use.
scenarios.reason: mstsc /v is a clear RDP-use signal but is common in legitimate administration. Treat as low-confidence technique telemetry unless additional context narrows it.

scenarios.description: Changing RDP Port to Non Standard Port via Powershell
evidence: Sysmon Event 1 captures Set-ItemProperty on HKLM SYSTEM CurrentControlSet Control Terminal Server WinStations RDP-Tcp PortNumber to 4489 and New-NetFirewallRule for TCP 4489.
No actual RDP client or completed RDP-session event is present in the selected five channels for this scenario.
scenarios.root_cause: The captured action is RDP service configuration, while the expected scenario technique is Remote Services: RDP. The available telemetry does not itself prove remote-service use.
scenarios.reason: Do not add a T1021.001 hit solely to improve this score unless the project explicitly decides that RDP-port configuration itself should map to that technique.

evidence: Sysmon Event 1 records WMIC.exe with command line wmic useraccount get /ALL /format:csv.
scenarios.root_cause: WMI query use is explicit, but existing T1047 rules cover WMI process creation, remote XSL execution, or WmiPrvSE child-process execution rather than reconnaissance queries.
scenarios.reason: A generic WMIC-query rule would increase technique coverage but can match legitimate administration. Benign frequency must be measured before adoption.

evidence: Sysmon Event 1 records WMIC.exe with command line wmic process get caption,executablepath,commandline /format:csv.
A WmiPrvSE.exe process is also present, but this scenario does not rely on the Security 4688 parent-child form used by the existing P2-10H rule.
scenarios.root_cause: WMI query use is explicit but outside the current T1047 rule shapes.
scenarios.reason: Same tradeoff as T1047-1: semantically valid WMI telemetry, but potentially noisy if any WMIC query is treated as suspicious.

scenarios.description: Create a new user in a command prompt
evidence: Security Event 4720 directly records creation of local account T1136.001_CMD.
Sysmon Event 1 also records net.exe user /add and net1.exe user /add.
scenarios.root_cause: Direct account-creation telemetry exists, but the 60-rule pack has no Security 4720 rule mapped to T1136.001.
scenarios.reason: Security 4720 is a generic, tool-independent account-creation event and covers the behavior without depending on Atomic-specific names or command syntax.

scenarios.description: Create a new user in PowerShell
evidence: Security Event 4720 directly records creation of local account T1136.001_PowerShell.
Sysmon Event 1 records PowerShell New-LocalUser -NoPassword.
scenarios.root_cause: Direct account-creation telemetry exists, but the 60-rule pack has no Security 4720 rule mapped to T1136.001.
scenarios.reason: The same Security 4720 rule can cover both account-creation scenarios without command- or tool-specific overfitting.

hold.reason: Available telemetry proves RDP configuration change, not an RDP remote-services session.
Current direct evidence is primarily the gsecdump tool invocation; avoid a tool-name-only rule.
Current direct evidence is primarily an NPPSpy-specific PowerShell configuration command and lacks a direct registry-change event in this capture.
